<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Serial-to-Parallel Conversion Circuit</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">Idle state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="RECEIVE">Receiving state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="OUTPUT">Output state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[3:0]">Counter to keep track of the number of received serial input data bits.</reg>
        <reg id="valid" width_description="[0:0]">Valid signal for the output data.</reg>
        <reg id="data" width_description="[7:0]">Data register to store the received serial input data.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 4'd0;
                valid <= 1'b0;
                data <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                case(cnt)
                    4'd0: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[7] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd1: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[6] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd2: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[5] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd3: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[4] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd4: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[3] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd5: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[2] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd6: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[1] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    4'd7: begin
                        if(din_valid == 1'b1) begin
                            data[0] <= din_serial;
                            cnt <= cnt + 1;
                        end
                    end
                    default: begin
                        cnt <= 4'd0;
                        valid <= 1'b1;
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        The module implements a serial-to-parallel conversion circuit. It receives a serial input signal "din_serial" along with a control signal "din_valid" indicating the validity of the input data. The module operates on the rising edge of the clock signal "clk" and uses a synchronous design. The input din_serial is a single-bit data, and when the module receives 8 input data, the output dout_parallel outputs the 8-bit data(The serial input values are sequentially placed in dout_parallel from the most significant bit to the least significant bit), and the dout_valid is set to 1.
    </implementation>
</module>
